producer_report.summary: Added an explicit hold state for open requests. `athena hold <job>` appends an `athena.hold/1` record (`<job>/hold-<n>.json`, state `on_hold`) and `athena release <job>` appends a later one (`released`); the highest `n` wins and the request record is untouched. `JobRecords::on_hold()` is true when the latest record is `on_hold` and the job is queued, proposed or dispatched. `RealSteps::entry_of` copies that into a new `PlanEntry.on_hold`, and `Plan::build_with` refuses such an entry first (reason "on hold; `athena release <id>` lifts it", empty `missing`) at any priority. Dependents are held by the existing dependency loop. `Drain::prepare` does not read an on-hold item, and `batches_for` drops everything in `plan.refused`, so drain never dispatches it. `athena plan` prints it as a `held` line, and `athena status` ends the line with "on hold" (new `JobLine.on_hold`, skipped in JSON when false). The error-review backfill (`backfill_step`) skips an on-hold request, so it is never closed and replaced by an unheld copy; the grep of `.close(` found that as the only automatic closer. The rejected-dependency rule from job 20261030-013323-nmnv (`job_history`, its tests) is untouched. Targeted tests, fmt and clippy pass. In the full `cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast` run one target fails: `design_surface` (see open_issues).

It asserts nothing is read, run or landed while the item is on hold, and that it is landed after release. `a_stub_drain_never_dispatches_an_on_hold_item_at_any_priority_and_dispatches_it_once_released` (Stub) does the same for all four levels, and `a_read_proposed_item_on_hold_is_not_dispatched_and_runs_once_released` covers a read job. The unit test `an_on_hold_item_is_not_planned_at_any_priority` is in plan.rs. All pass under `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain hold`. A read (proposed) job can be held. Passes. Note: refusing a closed job matches the criterion's 'non-queued job', but a read or interrupted job is deliberately allowed, per the accepted plan.

Deviation from the expected deliverables: `crates/athena-cli/tests/job_plan.rs` is unchanged on purpose. It covers the planner and critic roles of a job and never builds a PlanEntry, JobLine or hold. The hold tests sit beside the priority and focus tests in tests/drain.rs.
Addition beyond the deliverables, per the accepted plan: `crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs` gets the `backfill_step` skip for an on-hold request and one test. docs/records.md is not edited.

Limit: `athena status` reads the records worktree when it exists, while hold, release and drain read HEAD, as `athena priority` already does. The mark can lag a hold when the worktree is behind. The JobLine.on_hold doc comment says so, and the store test covers the worktree path.
A job that starts running after it was held (for example `athena go` on an on-hold job) is not stopped by the hold. `athena hold` itself refuses a job that is running now. Drain does not run it.
mistakes: My first full `cargo test --locked` run was sent to a file with shell redirection, which the policy denied; I reran with `--no-fail-fast` and `-q` to read the failure list.
learnings: `JobRecords::state()` turns Queued into Proposed as soon as a reading or invocation exists, so a hold tied to Queued would silently stop counting after `athena plan` reads the job. `on_hold()` therefore covers Queued, Proposed and Dispatched.
`Records::from_parts` panics on a record whose job `job_of` cannot name, so a new per-job record type needs an arm in `job_of` as well as in `JobRecords::add`.
`crates/athena-cli/tests/design_surface.rs` computes the inventory from the committed HEAD, not the working tree, so any new command makes it fail until the change is committed.
The only automatic caller of `Athena::close` is the error-review backfill's Requeue arm (hestia.rs, around line 2958); the other `.close(` hits in crates/ are tests or code-health span code.
desires: The test output file of a background cargo run, so a failure list could be read without rerunning the whole suite.
A way to run `design_surface` against the working tree; it reads the committed HEAD, so it cannot pass before the candidate is committed.
